c.tagline: A UNESCO-listed lantern-lit trading port frozen in time, where tailor shops and river cruises meet a nearby beach

card: Accepted at larger hotels and restaurants; cash preferred in the Ancient Town's shops and markets

taxi.fareNote: Grab is reliable; renting a bicycle is a popular way to reach An Bang Beach

emergency.note: 113 for police, 115 for medical emergencies; English support is decent given heavy tourism

religion: ancestor worship and folk traditions widely practiced alongside
walk: The Ancient Town is a pedestrian-friendly UNESCO site, best explored entirely on foot; An Bang Beach is a short bicycle or Grab ride away

safety.safety: Very safe town, popular with travelers of all ages
safety.crime: Petty theft and overcharging by unlicensed vendors in the Ancient Town are the main concerns

hood_landmark.Ancient Town (Old Quarter): The Japanese Covered Bridge and lantern-lit riverside streets
hood_landmark.An Bang Beach: An Bang Beach's row of beach bars and loungers
hood_landmark.Cam Thanh (Coconut Village): Cam Thanh's coconut palm forest and basket-boat rides
hood_landmark.Cam Nam Island: Cam Nam Island's quiet riverside cafes across the bridge
hood_landmark.New Town (Tan An): The newer commercial district beyond the Ancient Town

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the Ancient Town and night-market crowds, and expect persistent tailor and boat touts.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed heart of Hoi An, a car-free maze of lantern-strung streets, tailor shops, and centuries-old merchant houses; the essential base for any visit.
A relaxed beach a short bike ride from the Ancient Town, popular for sunset drinks and swimming.
A rural riverside village known for its round basket-boat rides through coconut palm channels, just outside town.
A quiet island across a small bridge from the Ancient Town, with a more local, low-key riverside feel.
The modern part of Hoi An beyond the historic core, with everyday shops and more affordable local dining.
lodging: AIRA Boutique Hoi An Hotels & Villa
NHAAN Resort & Spa Hoi An, Tapestry Collection by Hilton
Emerald Waters Hotel & Spa Hoi An

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water; tap water is not potable.

transit.sys: Bicycle rental (very popular), Grab, and local taxis
transit.hours: Roughly 6am-10pm for Grab; the Ancient Town restricts vehicle traffic in the evening
transit.map: Not centrally published; bicycle rental shops are everywhere
transit.note: Motorbikes and cars are restricted within the Ancient Town during certain hours; walking and cycling are the norm

transport.air: Da Nang International Airport (DAD), about 30-40 min away
transport.train: Da Nang railway station connects to the national rail network; a taxi/Grab covers the final leg to Hoi An
transport.bus: Local buses and shuttle services connect Da Nang and Hoi An
transport.car: Well connected via Highway 1 and the coastal road from Da Nang

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Viettel or Vinaphone tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for tour guides and tailors

food.name: Cao lau
food.desc: Hoi An's own noodle dish: chewy smoky noodles, slices of char siu pork, herbs, crisp croutons and just a splash of broth.

places.name: Cao Lau Thanh

places.name: Morning Glory Restaurant
places.note: Reliable sit-down version of every Hoi An classic; book for dinner.

places.name: Hoi An Central Market food court
places.note: Cheap bowls made fresh; go at lunch before stalls sell out.

food.name: White rose dumplings
food.desc: Banh bao banh vac: translucent rice-flour dumplings pinched into flower shapes around shrimp, topped with fried shallots.

places.name: Morning Glory Restaurant

food.desc: A crackling baguette stuffed with pate, cold cuts, herbs, pickles and house sauces; Hoi An is widely held to make the country's best.

places.name: Com Ga Huong
places.note: Smaller local shop with a punchier herb and chilli sauce.

places.name: Ba Le Well

places.name: Hoi An Central Market

food.name: Herbal tea and lotus tea

places.name: Reaching Out Tea House

places.name: Hoi An Roastery

landmarks: Japanese Covered Bridge (Chua Cau)
Hoi An's 400-year-old emblem, a rose-hued Japanese bridge with its own tiny temple, has linked the old town's merchant quarters since the 1590s.
Hoi An Ancient Town
This UNESCO-listed trading port of mustard-yellow shophouses, silk lanterns and cyclo-filled lanes preserves centuries of Vietnamese, Chinese and Japanese commerce in amber.
Fujian Assembly Hall (Phuc Kien)
The grandest of Hoi An's Chinese congregation halls dazzles with dragon mosaics, incense coils and a lavish gate honoring the sea goddess Thien Hau.
Tan Ky Old House
Seven generations of one merchant family have kept this 18th-century shophouse of dark timber, mother-of-pearl poetry and Japanese-Chinese-Vietnamese craftsmanship intact.
Thu Bon River Lantern Boats and Night Market
At dusk, sampans strung with silk lanterns glide past An Hoi's night market as visitors release candlelit paper flowers onto the darkened river.
Hoi An Central Market
Riverside stalls heap herbs, spices and cao lau noodles beside tailors and fishmongers, the fragrant working heart of Hoi An since its trading heyday.
An Bang Beach
A short bicycle ride through rice paddies ends at this laid-back stretch of pale sand, seafood shacks and views to the Cham Islands.
My Son Sanctuary
An hour inland, the jungle-wrapped brick towers of the Cham civilization's holiest site, built between the 4th and 13th centuries, form Vietnam's most evocative UNESCO ruins.
Tra Que Vegetable Village
Between town and beach, this centuries-old organic herb village invites visitors to hoe, plant and cook alongside farmers who supply Hoi An's kitchens.
Thanh Ha Pottery Village
On the riverbank west of town, potters have spun clay for 500 years, letting visitors throw a pot and browse a terracotta park of world monuments.

train.note: No international trains, and Hoi An has no station of its own. The nearest is Da Nang, about 40 minutes north by road, on the Reunification Express - the Da Nang to Hue leg over the Hai Van Pass is one of the great train rides in Asia. Book on dsvn.vn or through Baolau and take a taxi or shuttle for the last stretch.

bus.note: No international coaches from Hoi An itself - for Laos you travel via Da Nang or Hue. Open-tour sleeper buses run from the town to Hue (about 4 hours), Nha Trang and overnight to Ho Chi Minh City, operated by The Sinh Tourist (https://www.thesinhtourist.vn/) and others; book through Vexere (https://vexere.com/). Yellow local buses and endless private shuttles cover the Da Nang run.

intl.to: Cham Islands / Cu Lao Cham (Vietnam) - speedboat from Cua Dai, ~30 min, Mar-Sep
intl.op: local speedboat operators — tickets at Cua Dai pier

ferry.note: There are no international or long-distance sailings. The Cham Islands boats are the one real service, running from Cua Dai pier when the sea allows - typically March to September, with the route closed through the winter monsoon. Sampans on the Thu Bon river through the old town are sightseeing rides hired by the hour.

half.name: Da Nang
half.blurb: Coastal city with the Dragon Bridge and a long stretch of beach along the South China Sea.

half.name: Marble Mountains
half.blurb: Five limestone and marble hills with cave shrines and pagodas, climbed by stairs or elevator.

half.name: Cham Islands
half.blurb: Marine protected archipelago off the coast, reached by boat, known for snorkeling and coral reefs.

half.name: Ba Na Hills
half.blurb: Mountain resort reached by cable car, with a French colonial-style hill station and the Golden Bridge walkway.
